title: BPUFuzzer: Effective Fuzz Testing for Branching Transient Execution Vulnerabilities of RISC-V CPU
problem: Transient execution vulnerabilities (e.g., Spectre) in CPU branch prediction units are difficult to detect through traditional testing; existing fuzz testing approaches lack effective testcase generation for complex control flows and data extraction from vast RTL state spaces.
motivation: Spectre-type transient execution vulnerabilities pose severe security risks; automated detection during RTL design requires new testing methodologies that can systematically explore branch prediction behavior.
method: BPUFuzzer uses control flow graph-based testcase generation with anomaly detection to explore complex program flows and deliberately selects testcases using fitness and coverage metrics to discover transient execution vulnerabilities. It extracts essential data from hardware states to guide testcase selection.
key_novelty: First fuzz testing framework combining CFG-based testcase generation with anomaly detection and fitness-guided selection to systematically discover branching transient execution vulnerabilities in RTL.
contributions: Control flow graph-based testcase generation for complex branching behavior
Anomaly detection strategy for vulnerability symptom extraction from RTL states
Fitness and coverage metrics for effective testcase selection and prioritization
Discovery of multiple Spectre variants on RISC-V Boom v3, including novel Spectre-LOOP variant

metrics.other: discovery of previously unknown Spectre variant (Spectre-LOOP)

baselines: state-of-the-art transient execution vulnerability detection methods
primary_theme: Fuzz testing for transient execution vulnerabilities in CPUs
